tools.description: Send a free-form question to a Continuum agent, routed by the required `target`. For raw metric/number lookups (e.g. 'get IG metrics for @account', spend/ROAS/impressions for an account or campaign), call analytics_query directly — agent_ask is for interpretation, narrative reports, and multi-step analysis, not fetching a metric. Use when the question fits one of: target=jaina for performance/paid analytics, reporting, ROAS/spend/campaign/pacing questions; target=organic for social strategy, captions, content ideas, or organic post/account questions. Do NOT guess a target for a query about the other domain — the server validates `query` against `target` with a deterministic classifier and returns status=needs_correction (with suggested_target) instead of silently running the wrong agent on a confident mismatch; ambiguous or mixed-intent queries proceed as requested. Returns immediately with result.{ job_id, sessionId, poll_with } — poll jobs_status for the answer. The completed job result carries status: 'completed' when the run wrote a draft/plan, or status: 'needs_followup' when it produced text only; on needs_followup, send the next instruction with the SAME result.sessionId to continue the thread instead of restarting it. When target=organic ends holding an approval-gated plan the job result also carries { plan_id, pending_approval_token, placements } — commit that plan by calling organic_calendar_approve with those three (24h token, single use). Returns a structured needs_* result if the brand/role prerequisites are missing.

facts.terminalOutcome: Agent job (jaina or organic) enqueued; the answer is the terminal jobs_status result.

tools.name: brand_knowledge
tools.summary: Read and search everything Continuum knows about the active brand — the brand book, brand guidelines, the uploaded-document knowledge base, onboarding intake, and the structured p…
tools.description: Read and search everything Continuum knows about the active brand — the brand book, brand guidelines, the uploaded-document knowledge base, onboarding intake, and the structured profile. Use it to ground yourself in the brand before writing content or analyzing performance. action=overview lists what is available (readiness, guideline purposes, document counts by category, onboarding status, profile sections). Read `brand_book.alignment_claimable` before you write anything: when it is false this brand has no verifiable brand book, and you MUST NOT describe your output as "aligned to the brand book" — say what you actually grounded it in and surface the returned `warning`. `documents.unclassified` counts documents still filed as misc; while it equals the total, the `categories` search filter cannot match anything. action=search runs semantic search over the uploaded knowledge base (`query`; optional `categories` filter such as brand_guidelines/creative_strategy/audience_persona/product_info; add `sources` — any of ['documents','guidelines','brand_report'] — to also search brand guideline tags and brand-report vectors). action=read fetches a whole artifact via `source`: brand_book (DNA + readiness; add `full:true` for the full brand.md), guidelines (structured colors/typography/verbal identity; optional `purpose`), onboarding (intake answers), or profile (voice/pmf/audience/persona + context; optional `section`). action=validate checks `copy` for a `platform` against the brand's voice rules. WRITES (operator role): action=add_text stores agent-authored markdown as a document (`name`, `text`); action=add_url ingests an https document by URL (`name`, `url`; a Google Drive/Docs/Slides link works when shared as 'Anyone with the link'). Both accept `category` and `retention` — omit `category` and the document is classified from its name and content (the result reports what it was filed as); retention=ephemeral scopes it to THIS session and expires it in 14 days. action=add_file accepts a small (up to 5 MiB) PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, CSV, text or supported image as padded file_base64 with file_name and mime_type; it returns a documentId for Forge drafts. For a larger file (up to 50 MB, e.g. a PDF brand book) when you can run a shell: action=upload_url (`file_name`, `mime_type`) returns a put_url and curl line; PUT the bytes, then action=upload_finalize (`upload_path`, optional `name`/`category`) ingests it like a web upload. action=update renames or re-categorizes (`document_id`, `name`, `category`; pass `expected_updated_at` to avoid clobbering a concurrent edit). action=archive takes a document down and is two-phase: call it once for a preview + confirm_token, then again with mode='confirm'. action=restore undoes an archive. action=save_permanent promotes an ephemeral document to brand-wide permanent knowledge. action=document_status polls ingest progress after a write. Returns a structured needs_* result if no brand is selected.

facts.terminalOutcome: Per action: brand book / guidelines / knowledge-base / onboarding / profile read or searched, or copy validated; or the knowledge base mutated — a text/URL/direct-file document created and queued for extract-chunk-embed, a document renamed or re-categorized under a stale-write guard, a document archived (preview then confirm, reversible) or restored, or an ephemeral session-scoped document promoted to permanent brand-wide knowledge.

tools.description: Create and ship organic content (the full write lifecycle) to the platforms with a real publisher. action=draft (requires `platform`) returns a draftId for a caption/plan post (generate=false mints a bare stub, and with generate=false you may pass `caption` / `hashtags` to store copy that was already written and approved — it is saved verbatim, nothing is regenerated); action=extend edits a draft — pass `updates` for a structured field change (scheduled_date/slot_data/content_json, trial_reel to publish an Instagram reel to non-followers first, or status back to draft/placeholder; approved/scheduled/published/failed are owned by the approve+publish actions) OR `prompt` for a natural-language rewrite (e.g. 'rewrite the caption in Mexican Spanish'), which runs the organic agent in place and returns a poll handle; action=realize generates the creative — two-phase like the other spending writes: call it with the draftId alone to get back the draft's `preview_revision` plus the storyboard frames it covers (state=awaiting_preview_approval), then call it again with that `preview_revision` to approve those frames and generate (state=generating); a draft with no storyboard yet gets one built first (state=previewing). tools.description: Change the brand’s Forge render sets and render them. A render set is rows of variable values for ONE template; a row with parentId inherits its parent’s values and overrides some (a variation). Read first with forge_query. action='set_create' (templateKey, bindingId when the key is in two workspaces, name, rows[{label, overrides, parentId}], description) — row ids are minted when omitted. 'set_update' (setId, expectedRevision from forge_query set, and any of name/description/rows/settings — rows REPLACES the whole list). settings (set_create/set_update; only the keys named change, null clears) are the set's delivery defaults: metaTarget {adAccountId, campaignId, adsetId} — a new PAUSED ad in that ad set for every row without its own target (ids from forge_query destinations and paid_manage action=hierarchy; replacing an existing ad stays a per-row delivery), slackDestinationId, approvalDestinationIds, final. 'set_fork' (setId, name optional) copies a set into a new one. 'set_delete' (setId). 'suggest_rows' drafts rows with AI (brief or documentIds/mediaAssetIds; setId or templateKey; count ceiling and autoCount; varyKeys; parentRowId) and saves NOTHING. Use brand_knowledge action=add_file for small documents, library_manage action=upload_inline for small images, or source_begin for a signed-in upload handoff (documents, images, videos, and template projects: an After Effects package or ZIP, PSD, AI, PowerPoint, HTML, .blend); source_status returns documentIds, mediaAssetIds and templateAssetIds when ready. 'source_figma' (figmaUrl: a Figma frame link imports that frame; a file link lists its frames, then figmaNodeIds up to 5) makes each frame a design template with the brand's Figma connection: a web component that renders as its templateKey (web:<assetId>) with no build. 'apply_suggestions' (setId, expectedRevision, selected rows with their draft ids) appends selected rows once, preserving the rest of the set. 'render_preview' (setId, rowIds optional) checks every row as the Render tab does and returns readiness, destinations (where each row goes: library, new_ad, replace) and a single-use confirmationToken. Omitted slackDestinationId/approvalDestinationIds/final take the set's settings (slackDestinationId null = no post); a row's own delivery wins over the set's metaTarget; anything bound for Meta parks for approval; final=true is a non-proof render, owner/admin only. A refusal a person may override names its flag (acceptMissingFonts, acceptLinkedLineMismatch, acceptOffPaletteColor) in details.overrides — ask the person before passing it. 'render_confirm' (confirmationToken) queues the renders and returns a batchId; wait with forge_query action='batch' from a background subagent. Refusals keep the service's reason (e.g. render_set_revision_conflict: re-read the set). 'rows_patch' (setId, expectedRevision, rows upserted by id — no id appends — and removeRowIds). 'set_create' and 'set_retarget' (setId, expectedRevision) take templateRevisionId, a PUBLISHED revision; 'set_fork' takes revision, a kept state. Templates (forge_query template_tree, template_layers first): 'template_preview' (assetId, parentRevisionId, edits{layers[{compId, layerId, text|font|fontSize|visible|x|y|width|height|rotation|scale|opacity}], slots[{slotKey, defaultValue|publicName|required|exposed|charBudget}], orders[{compId, layerIds}], recolor{palette}}) saves nothing; 'template_save' (the same plus name, a new variant, OR variantId whose head is parentRevisionId) commits; the Original is never rewritten. Owner/admin: 'template_forge' (assetId: the revision's sourceAssetId; step start with templateName, decisions, draft, smoke, promote, resume) publishes it — after start the autopilot smokes and publishes on its own when nothing needs a person, so step in only where template_run parks; a CONFLICT means the run already moved; smoke renders cost money; 'template_set_default' (assetId, variantId). 3D product scenes (forge_query action='scenes'): 'scene_fill' (assetId, versionId, brief{productImageAssetId, headline, price, cta, text}, outputs optional) fills the scene from the brand — logo, palette, a product picture — and the brief, renders NOTHING, and returns the values plus a single-use confirmationToken; 'scene_render' (confirmationToken) queues one render per output into the Library. Poll with the template's scene render history in the Forge.

Valid tag ids are the `value`s intel_competitor_moves returns. tools.description: What are the brand's tracked competitors doing? A digest over their PAID ads and ORGANIC posts in a window (default the last 90 days): one row per competitor × tag dimension (angle, hook, cta, format) × value, with paid {ads, active, medianDaysRunning} and organic {posts, outlierShare = share of scored posts that earned ≥2× the account's median engagement}, plus exemplarSnapshotIds (open with intel_competitor_ads snapshotId) and exemplarPostIds (the postId intel_competitor_organic returns). Rows with many long-running active ads are what a competitor keeps paying for; a high outlierShare is what lands organically. Call this FIRST for 'what angles/hooks/offers are competitors using', then open exemplars with the list tools. Read coverage before concluding: many untagged items mean the tagger has not reached them yet, not that competitors are quiet. trackedCompetitorCount 0 means nothing is tracked (intel_competitor_ads returns onboarding recommendations). Deterministic over stored tags — no model, no live Meta fetch. Narrow with competitorRef, dimensions, source (paid|organic). Refresh or track new competitors with intel_competitor_scan. stillProcessing > 0 means a scan is still analyzing that many ads: the result is partial, so present it as such and offer to check again shortly. Dimensions (one tag taxonomy shared by paid ads and organic posts): angle = the strategic selling angle the creative leads with; hook = how it opens; cta = what it asks the viewer to do (none = asks nothing); format = what kind of creative it is.

tools.name: library_manage
tools.summary: Browse and manage the brand's media library as a creative system of record: review workflow state, comment threads with annotations, and version history. action=browse lists asset…
tools.description: Browse and manage the brand's media library as a creative system of record: review workflow state, comment threads with annotations, and version history. action=browse lists assets with filters (`reviewStatus` e.g. 'approved' to use only signed-off creative, `kind`, `source`, `tags`, `limit`≤50, `offset`) — add `query` to rank semantically instead of newest-first; items include a short-lived signed URL and an open (unresolved) comment count. action=asset_detail returns one asset in full: metadata + signed URL, every live comment thread (with box/timestamp annotations), version history, the last 20 review events, and its CREATIVE DNA — every Meta ad and organic post this creative ran in, per-version rollups (spend/impressions/CTR/ROAS/purchases + organic reach), a plain-language read of the v(n) vs v(n-1) delta, and what was generated from it. Answers "which version of this creative is winning and where is it running?" in ONE call (optional `window`: d7 | d14 | d30, default d30). Every rollup carries `trustFlags` + `trustNotes`: `low_evidence` = below the $50/3,000-impression floor (directional only), `inferred_link` = the ad↔asset link is a visual-embedding GUESS so the figures may belong to a DIFFERENT creative, `unknown_version` = we cannot tell which cut ran. NEVER quote a flagged figure as proven. action=import_ad_creative (operator) turns a SYNCED Meta ad creative (`creativeRowId` = paid_media.ad_creatives.id) into a real Library asset so it can be commented on, versioned and reviewed like any other creative, and links it back to the ad it came from. Idempotent: re-importing returns the same asset. action=upload_inline (operator) stores 1-8 JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF/AVIF images supplied as strict padded base64 (10 MiB each, 40 MiB total) and returns pinned `{asset_id,version_id}` Library references. Supply `operation_id` for an explicit replay identity; an identical payload derives one automatically. To put a file the user gave you into the Library, prefer in this order: (1) action=upload_url (operator) when you can run a shell (Claude Code, Desktop, a code sandbox with network): pass `uploads: [{file_name, mime_type}]` (1-8, any image/video/audio/document, 500 MiB each), PUT each file's bytes to its `put_url` (the returned `curl` line), then action=upload_finalize (operator) with `uploaded: [{upload_path}]` returns pinned Library references — no second upload by the user. (2) action=upload_inline for a small image you hold as base64. (3) action=upload_begin (operator) when you cannot reach the bytes: a 24-hour signed-in web handoff that opens the Library on this brand; any Library upload the user makes there completes it, and action=upload_status (viewer) with `upload_intent_id` returns the pinned references. action=comment_add (operator) leaves feedback: `assetId` + `body`, optional `annotation` ({kind:"box",…} image region, {kind:"time",timeMs} video moment, or {kind:"time",timeMs,endMs} video time RANGE for feedback about a passage) and `parentCommentId` to reply in a thread. Comments are NOT deduped by content — a blind retry writes a second comment, so pass `operation_id` if you may retry. action=set_review_status (operator) moves an asset through review (`toStatus`: none | draft | in_review | needs_changes | approved, optional `note`) and records the transition in the audit trail. Pass `expectedCurrentStatus` (the status you last saw) so the call is REJECTED rather than overwriting a decision someone made in the meantime; a transition to the status the asset already holds is a no-op (`changed:false`), not a new audit event. Use media_search when you only need to FIND creative by meaning; use this tool for review state and feedback. NOT available here yet (do these in the Continuum web app): editing/resolving/deleting comments, creating or restoring versions, collections, tags, custom fields, share links, and bulk operations. Returns a structured needs_* result if prerequisites are missing.

facts.terminalOutcome: Library state read or moved per action: assets browsed/filtered, one asset returned in full (comments + versions + review trail + Creative DNA), a comment persisted, a review transition recorded in the audit trail, or a synced Meta ad creative materialized as a Library asset linked back to the ad it came from.

tools.description: Manage the paid-media optimizer for the active brand (the budget-reallocation engine over Meta ad sets). action='create_portfolio' opens a portfolio (brand_id, ad_account_id, config: name/objective/level/mode/apply_mode/daily_total); 'create_from_suggestion' runs the onboarding flow — create + enroll — from a suggestion returned by optimizer_query action='suggestions'; 'enroll_adsets' enrolls ad sets (adset_ids) OR a whole campaign's ad sets (campaign_id — e.g. right after converting a CBO campaign) and queues the first cycle; 'convert_cbo' converts a CBO (campaign-budget) campaign to ad-set budgets so the optimizer can manage it — TWO-PHASE: mode='preview' (default) returns the computed per-ad-set budgets plus a confirm_token and writes nothing to Meta; mode='apply' with that confirm_token performs the real write; 'set_recommendation_status' approves/rejects ONE engine recommendation (portfolio_id + recommendation_id; the pending row IS the preview, so there is no confirm step — instead the write is refused if the row already moved out of expected_status, and re-approving returns the same receipt). Approving a fatigue rec opens a renewal task, whose id comes back in the receipt; 'set_recommendation_statuses' approves/rejects many at once and returns an ITEMIZED {applied[], skipped[{id,reason}]} — a bad or stale id is skipped, never hidden behind a count; 'set_renewal_task_status' closes a renewal work item (open|done|dismissed) with the same stale-state precondition; 'update_portfolio' edits portfolio settings (apply_mode='autopilot' is refused here — arming autonomous budget writes is a dashboard act); 'archive_portfolio' stops future optimization cycles (it does NOT pause any ad); 'unenroll_adsets' removes ad sets; 'run_now' triggers a reallocation cycle immediately for one portfolio_id (refused on an armed autopilot portfolio, whose cycle would write real Meta budgets; returns service_unreachable if the optimizer service is offline — the cycle still runs on its schedule). This tool does not pause or activate ads, ad sets or campaigns. Pausing is paid_manage action=update_entity (status PAUSED), preview → confirm, so the user confirms every pause; activating there also needs an admin's mcp_approval_grant. Use optimizer_query to read portfolios, performance, suggestions, and outcomes. Returns a structured needs_* result if a prerequisite (brand/role/integration) is missing. Full per-action input schema: help_describe { tool: "optimizer_manage", action }.

facts.terminalOutcome: Optimizer state mutated per action (portfolio created, ad sets enrolled, recommendation acted on, cycle run) via optimizer_* RPCs.

tools.description: Manage paid media on Meta ads (and Google Ads via action=google_ads). Read: hierarchy (campaigns/ad sets/ads with budgets, targeting, deleted ads on request), activity (audit log of every paid write: who, request, result). Write: create_campaign (optionally with ad sets and ads in one go), create_adset (radius/geo, age, gender, interests, audiences, placements, optimization goal, destination incl. WhatsApp, budget, schedule), create_ad, upload_media, update_entity (budget, bid, bid strategy, optimization goal, name, schedule, targeting, placements, status PAUSED/ACTIVE/ARCHIVED), update_ad_copy, duplicate, create_audience, create_lookalike, create_customer_list_audience, delete_audience, send_conversions (Conversions API, incl. offline), manage_rules (Meta automated rules), google_ads, guardrails (spend caps). Campaigns, ad sets, ads and copies are created PAUSED. Every write is two-phase: params.mode='preview' returns a diff + confirm_token (10 min), then mode='confirm'. Activating (incl. creating an ENABLED Meta rule), raising a budget past the brand's guardrails (default +30%), or a brand with an approval chain needs an admin to call mcp_approval_grant on the token. action=batch previews many writes under ONE confirm_token. Each write receipt returns `undo` — the paid_manage call that reverses it, or null + the reason when Meta cannot (sent conversions, archive). Organic-post boost is not supported. tools.name: studio_workflow
tools.summary: Co-pilot the AI Studio canvas. action=get reads one source: workflow_id for a saved library template, room_id for a real workspace, or the active workspace when neither is supplie…
tools.description: Co-pilot the AI Studio canvas. action=get reads one source: workflow_id for a saved library template, room_id for a real workspace, or the active workspace when neither is supplied; every Canvas read returns room_id. action=build is workspace-first: target='canvas' is the default, requires room_id, and creates a workflow from typed node specs + simple connections. Use explicit target='library' only to save a reusable template. Do not guess node specs: call help_describe { tool: 'studio_workflow' } first for the node_vocabulary field — the 28 node types with their handles, models, sizes and wiring rules. To make the creative for a Planner draft, pass `source_draft_id` instead of hand-written nodes: build reads that draft for its visual prompt and format, seeds prompt → generator (at the format's delivery ratio) → plannerDraft with targetDraftId already set, and writes it into that draft's own workspace. action=workspace_list returns the real Canvas workspaces users see after login; action=workspace_create creates one through the same brand workspace store and returns its room_id + open_url. A brand may hold at most three workspaces: when workspace_create reports CONFLICT, free one with action=workspace_delete { room_id } — a destructive two-phase call that removes the workspace and its canvas, refuses the reserved Planner workspace and refuses the last one standing. action=edit requires an explicit target. target=canvas requires room_id and writes that real workspace; use seed_workflow_id to merge a saved workflow first. target=library requires workflow_id + expected_updated_at and version-guards the saved workflow update. Surgical ops include add_node, remove_node, update_node, connect, disconnect, rewire, attach_library_asset, attach_unsplash_photo, attach_media, detach_media, rename. attach_library_asset accepts the stable `{asset_id,version_id}` returned by library_manage and resolves storage server-side. attach_unsplash_photo `{id, photo_id}` puts an unsplash_search photo on an image node as a hotlinked reference with its photographer credit. action=save writes a named Canvas room back to an existing saved workflow with expected_updated_at; action=save_as_copy explicitly creates a new saved workflow from either room_id or workflow_id. Every mutation returns a read-back graph_hash plus `persisted`: true when everything you asked for landed, false when part of it was refused — a refused part also makes the envelope status 'partial' and names itself in `rejected` (edit) or `unresolved` (build). action=run requires room_id and needs no human at a browser: when a canvas is open ANYWHERE in the brand it runs there, and when none is, the server generates the image/video nodes headlessly and files the media back onto the canvas. With `node_ids`, unrun upstream generators run first, as on the canvas. A scope of action nodes (image.blur, image.crop, …) runs too, one recipe per final action. When PART of the scope needs the browser the rest still runs: the envelope status is 'partial' and `blocked_by` names each skipped node and why. needs_open_canvas is returned only when NOTHING in scope is runnable. run_status resolves the original run's stored room even if the user switches workspaces, and reports `media_refs` and `previews` with the node_id that produced each one. A server-side run is bounded: one run at a time per room (a second call returns status='already_running', started=false, with the in-flight run's handle — nothing new is generated), and at most a handful of generator nodes per call — a wider scope returns status='too_many_nodes' with the cap, so scope it with `node_ids`. Server runs are limited to 10 per brand per clock hour (open-canvas runs do not count); each reports runs_remaining, and a spent budget returns RATE_LIMITED with retry_after_seconds, so batch nodes into one run. action=rename and action=delete manage a saved library workflow (delete is destructive → two-phase). Publisher sinks (plannerDraft/organicPublish/paidPublisher/apiRender) are terminal DELIVERY HANDOFFS: a run never executes them, so get/build/run/run_status report them under `publisher_handoffs` — deliver with the studio_deliver tool. For action=build, target='canvas' writes to the live room the user is viewing (changes appear instantly) while target='library' saves a reusable workflow. The user may be editing the same canvas at the same time, so canvas writes are additive: build adds its nodes alongside whatever is already there, and mode='replace' (build only) is the explicit, destructive opt-in that clears the canvas first. DESTRUCTIVE requests — build mode='replace', and edit with remove_node/disconnect/detach_media — are two-phase: the first call returns status='confirmation_required' with a confirm_token naming exactly what would be removed, and only a repeat of that same call carrying the token executes it. Every other action is additive and needs no token. Returns a structured needs_* result if prerequisites are missing.

facts.terminalOutcome: Workflow graph read/built/edited (canvas or library); destructive branches (build mode='replace', edit remove_node/disconnect/detach_media, delete) require a preview + confirm_token; `run` executes async on a live canvas via run_status; saved workflows can be renamed/deleted; publisher sinks report publisher_handoffs — deliver via studio_deliver.

tools.name: video_editor
tools.summary: Edit Video Studio projects — the same timeline the person has open in the Continuum editor, which refreshes live after every edit. Set `action` to an operation below and pass that…
tools.description:
Edit Video Studio projects — the same timeline the person has open in the Continuum editor, which refreshes live after every edit. Set `action` to an operation below and pass that operation’s fields alongside it. Times are seconds on the output timeline. Preserve explicitly requested options, including start time and duration; optional means the person may omit a setting, not that their request may be ignored. For set_captions, highlight is "none", "word", or "karaoke"; style is a separate field. export starts a render job that makes a Library MP4; poll export_status for its download URL. Every action except list_projects and create_project requires projectId in its arguments, even after reading get_project. When a projectId is supplied, use it; only list_projects when no project is identified. Read get_project as needed; timeline edits return the new revision, and undo restores the one before. Reading a project does not complete an edit: perform the requested write before reporting it done. Answers that name a project carry `editorUrl`, the page to open to watch it. Operations:
- list_workflows: List this brand's saved editing workflows and the house effects (/shoulder-zoom, /glass-graph, …). Each is a name and a prompt: to run one, carry out its prompt on the CURRENT project with the named editor operations. They are reusable instructions, not fixed clip IDs. Required: projectId.
- save_workflow: Save reusable editing instructions in the brand workflow library, without changing the timeline. Use general instructions about the current footage or selected clips; do not freeze project IDs or clip IDs. Saving does not run the instructions. Required: projectId, name, prompt.
- list_projects: List the brand's video projects, most recently edited first, each with the path of its editor so a person can open it. Options: limit.
- create_project (edits): A new project from Library videos (e.g. media_upload_and_clip's source_asset_id), laid on the main track in the order given; preset formats it. Returns the projectId — then draft_cut, then export. Required: assetIds. Options: title, preset.
- get_project: Read the timeline: tracks, clips (ids, timing, source assets, text), markers including beat markers, format, and the revision + fingerprint every edit must name. Pass full=true for the complete project document. Required: projectId. Options: full.
- get_transcript: Every spoken word on the timeline, mapped to timeline time through each clip’s trim and speed. Pass clipId for one clip. Required: projectId. Options: clipId.
- get_beats (edits): Detect the beat grid of the music on the timeline (or of clipId) and persist it as beat markers. Returns beat times on the timeline. Re-uses existing beat markers unless force=true. Required: projectId. Options: clipId, force.
- get_frame: A picture of the topmost visible video clip at a timeline time, so you can look before you cut. Required: projectId, timeSec. Options: maxWidth.
- apply_commands (edits): Apply raw editor commands (add_track, upsert_clip, move_clip, trim_clip, split_clip, set_keyframes, upsert_transition, set_export_settings, upsert_marker, …) atomically. Omit commandId/idempotencyKey/expectedRevision/issuedAt/actor — they are filled in. Fails closed if expectedRevision is stale: read the project again and retry. Required: projectId, expectedRevision, commands.
- undo (edits): Restore the timeline to an earlier revision (default: the one before the current). Undo is itself a new revision, so it can be undone. Required: projectId. Options: toRevision.
- cut_silence (edits): Remove pauses and dead air (ripple), keeping a little breath around every word. Scope to one clip with clipId. Required: projectId. Options: clipId, minSilenceSec, paddingSec, thresholdDb.
- cut_ranges (edits): Cut exact timeline ranges out of every track. With ripple (default) everything after closes the gap. Required: projectId, ranges. Options: ripple.
- beat_cut (edits): Make rhythmic cuts: jump_cuts skips footage from one forward primary clip and shortens the timeline while preserving authored motion and gain curves. It protects speech/captions and keeps music-bed audio continuous; speech protection can prevent cuts. The range must stay inside that clip without overlapping transitions; reversed or speed-ramped clips in the affected range are refused. switch_shots alternates at least two distinct source spans with original audio continuous. everyNBeats 0.5 or 0.25 makes half/quarter-beat cuts. cut_on_beat only splits for edit preparation. audioClipId redetects the beat source; it does not label narration as music. Required: projectId. Options: mode, everyNBeats, clipIds, audioClipId, range.
- collage (edits): Show two to four existing picture clips together in filled collage panels, without replacing the main sequence or its audio. stack makes horizontal strips, side_by_side makes columns, grid needs four clips. Each panel uses a centered crop. One undo removes the collage. Required: projectId, clipIds. Options: layout, atSec, durationSec.
- set_captions (edits): Write word-timed animated captions from the speech on the timeline into a caption track, replacing existing auto-captions. Required: projectId. Options: style, highlight, maxWordsPerLine, position, highlightColor.
- set_speed (edits): Change a video, audio or composition clip to a constant playback rate, keeping its source span and scaling its own automation. Main-video changes repack the sequence and carry its captions and overlays; composition changes retain other instances and the child sequence. Reverse and speed ramps are not supported. One undo restores the edit. Required: projectId, clipId, rate. Options: expectedRevision.
- edit_caption_cues (edits): Correct spelling in existing timed caption cues without regenerating captions or changing word timing, confidence or emphasis. Each replacement must have the same number of words. Get full project data for cue IDs first. All corrections commit together and undo together. Required: projectId, cues. Options: expectedRevision.
- get_composed_frame: See the actual composed timeline frame, including text, captions, overlays, transitions and looks. Use after visual edits to verify the result; get_frame reads source footage only. Required: projectId, timeSec. Options: maxWidth.
- set_format (edits): Switch the project to a platform format (TikTok/Reels/Shorts 9:16, YouTube 16:9, square, 4:5) and refit unlocked, centered full-frame video clips to cover (fill, crop edges) or contain (fit, letterbox). Preserve authored positioning, pivots, motion and 3D transforms. Required: projectId, preset. Options: fit.
- add_text (edits): Add animated text: a template (hook_title, lower_third, kinetic_words, cta_end_card, listicle_number, quote, stat_callout, subtitle_bar — two-layer templates take secondaryText) or a plain title, lower third, kinetic line or call to action. animationIn/animationOut override the entrance and exit. Required: projectId, text, startSec. Options: kind, template, secondaryText, durationSec, animationIn, animationOut, style.
- add_clip (edits): Place a Library or pool asset on the timeline at a time: video on a video track, an image as an overlay, audio on an audio track. versionId keeps a specific stored version; omit it to use the current head. sourceInSec/durationSec trim it; newTrack puts it on a track of its own. Required: projectId, assetId. Options: versionId, atSec, trackId, newTrack, sourceInSec, durationSec.
- animate_clip (edits): Animate any visual clip (video, overlay, text) with a motion preset: fade/slide/pop/spring/zoom in at its start, fade/slide out at its end, punch_in or shake at atSec (timeline seconds), or ken_burns across the whole clip. Replaces the clip's keyframes of the same properties in that window. Required: projectId, clipId, preset. Options: durationSec, atSec.
- get_motion: Read the keyframes of the keyframed clips (or of clipIds), each in timeline seconds, with the clip start and length. Read it before keyframe_clip, stagger_clips or retime_motion. Required: projectId. Options: clipIds.
- keyframe_clip (edits): Write keyframes for one property of one clip: each key is { t (timeline seconds), v } — or { t, x, y } for transform.position, a normalized canvas point (0.5, 0.5 is the centre) — with an optional ease name, or bezier [x1, y1, x2, y2] for a custom curve. replace=true clears that property first; otherwise each key replaces only the key at its time. For a ready-made entrance or exit use animate_clip. Required: clipId, property, keys, projectId. Options: parameterName, effectInstanceId, replace.
- stagger_clips (edits): "Stagger these": move the selected clips so each starts eachSec after the previous, in the order given (the on-screen order of the selection; from=end or center reorders the offsets). Refuses clips on the main video track. One undo restores them. Required: clipIds, eachSec, projectId. Options: from.
- retime_motion (edits): "Snappier", "slower", "bouncier": shift (shiftSec), rescale to durationSec, and/or re-ease the keyframes of the selected clips — every keyframed property, or one. The clips themselves do not move. Re-ease with an ease name, or bezier [x1, y1, x2, y2] for a custom curve. Required: clipIds, projectId. Options: property, shiftSec, durationSec, ease, bezier.
- add_hyperframes_clip (edits): Place a HyperFrames composition (its revisionId) on its own overlay track as a transparent film at atSec, linked to the revision so get_hyperframes_clip_motion and edit_hyperframes_clip_motion can read and change its animations. Renders the film first, which takes a while. Required: revisionId, projectId. Options: atSec, trackId, newTrack.
- add_motion_graphic (edits): Compose a ready-made motion graphic (recipe glass_graph, particle_push, dot_matrix or word_lock) from the words and figures given, and place it at atSec on an overlay track for durationSec as a transparent HyperFrames film — its entrances stay editable with edit_hyperframes_clip_motion. Renders the film first, which takes a while. Required: recipe, projectId. Options: atSec, durationSec, color, label, value, unit, points, steps, words, keyword, lines, text, cards, lightSpeed, faceX, faceWidth, eyeY, trackId, newTrack.
- get_hyperframes_clip_motion: Read the animations inside a HyperFrames clip: each animation's id, label, targets (data-hf-id), start and end in composition seconds, stagger and properties, with compositionStartSec to place them on the timeline. Read it before edit_hyperframes_clip_motion. Required: clipId, projectId.
- edit_hyperframes_clip_motion (edits): "Stagger the headline", "make the CTA snappier" inside a HyperFrames clip: apply motion ops to its composition (only the named animations change), re-render the film, and point every clip showing it at the new render. One undo restores the previous film. Use stagger_clips or retime_motion for ordinary clips. Required: clipId, opsJson, projectId.
- add_transition (edits): The only way to add or remove a transition. Joins fromClipId to the next clip on the main video track (crossfade, dip to black or white, wipe, slide, zoom); type cut removes it. blur is not available yet. all=true joins EVERY neighbouring pair of the main track with that type and length, leaving pairs too short for it as cuts — "a clean transition between the clips" is one call with all=true and no fromClipId. Do not build one with apply_commands, and do not move clips to make it fit. Required: projectId, type. Options: fromClipId, toClipId, all, durationSec.
- apply_effect (edits): Give a video or overlay clip a look: a filter (bw, vintage, vivid, cool, warm, noir, dream) or an effect (blur, tint, vignette, film_grain, dust, light_leaks, chromatic_aberration, vhs, pixelate, corner_radius, chroma_key) at a strength 0–1; remove takes it off. Required: projectId, clipId, effect. Options: strength, color, remove.
- draft_cut (edits): Turn the project's footage and a goal into first cuts: reads every spoken line, picks and orders the strongest ones for the goal (a hook, a testimonial, a highlight, a story, a demo) at the target length, then captions and formats each cut. Finishing, each opt-in: music (a bed ducked under speech; musicPrompt sets its mood), hookTitle (a short headline over the opening), broll (cutaways from the pool's footage without speech over body lines) and brandCaptions (captions in the brand's type and colours) — turn them on unless the person asked for a bare cut. Variant A replaces this timeline (undoable); B, C… open as sibling projects. Returns a jobId — poll draft_cut_status. Required: projectId, brief. Options: kind, targetDurationSec, variants, preset, captions, sourceAssetIds, music, musicPrompt, hookTitle, broll, brandCaptions.
- draft_cut_status: Progress of a draft_cut; when completed, each variant with its project, length, angle and the lines it used. Required: projectId, jobId.
- list_variants: The sibling cuts drafted from the same brief as this project (A, B, C…), for switching between variants. Required: projectId.
- export: Render the timeline to an MP4 on the render service and save it to the Library. Poll export_status with the returned jobId. Required: projectId. Options: preset, captionMode.
- export_status: Progress of an export; when completed, the Library asset and a download URL. Required: projectId, jobId.
- get_pool: Media available to this edit: assets wired into it on the canvas graph, the project’s own sources, and generated results. Required: projectId.
- generate: Generate media from a quick start and optionally place it on the timeline; poll generate_status. Pictures and clips: create/restyle/edit image, storyboard or keyframes to video, 360 rotation (reference assets in refs). music_bed: an instrumental bed from prompt (mood, genre, tempo) on an audio track, as long as the timeline unless durationSec, ducked under speech unless duck=false. voiceover: prompt is the exact script to speak, voice the delivery (e.g. "warm, confident, Mexican Spanish"), placed on an audio track at place.atSec. headless_concept: a finished reel of the brand's approved cast made from concept (street-interview, pov, unpopular-opinion, problem-solution…) with prompt as the angle, placed as video. Required: projectId, quickStart. Options: prompt, refs, preset, place, voice, durationSec, concept, duck.
- generate_status: Progress of a generation; when completed, the new asset and the clip it was placed as. Required: projectId, jobId.

facts.terminalOutcome: A Video Studio project read (timeline, transcript, beats, a frame) or edited as one committed revision the open editor refetches live (cut pauses/ranges, beat cuts, word-timed captions, platform format, text, undo); export renders on Continuum Render into a Library MP4 polled through export_status.

recipe.description: glass_graph: a liquid glass card that refracts the footage under it while a line graph climbs to a figure (label, value, unit, points). particle_push: particles pour into a box that opens into up to 3 numbered steps (steps). dot_matrix: words in LED dots, one after another (words). word_lock: newspaper pages cut fast with one highlighted word locked in the centre (keyword, lines). screen_push: cuts to an extreme close-up of a monitor that shows the exact words, hard-cutting to each word as the speaker says it (text; it times itself from the transcript). over_shoulder: the camera pushes in, looks to a card over one shoulder, whips to a card over the other, then pulls back, 4.6 s (cards, faceX, faceWidth, eyeY, lightSpeed).

anyOf.description: The accent as #RRGGBB: the glass_graph line, the screen_push letters, the over_shoulder outline; omit for the brand accent

value.description: glass_graph: the figure the graph climbs to

points.description: glass_graph: the line, 2–12 values in order; omit for a steady climb

steps.description: particle_push: 1–3 step labels of one or two words

words.description: dot_matrix: 1–6 words, shown one after another

keyword.description: word_lock: the one word locked in the centre

lines.description: word_lock: 3–10 sentences, each containing the keyword

cards.description: over_shoulder: the start card (over the left shoulder) then the end card, each { label, big, small } — "BEFORE" | "$3,200" | "per month"

lightSpeed.description: over_shoulder: the start card's big text flies into the end card at light speed

faceX.description: over_shoulder: the middle of the face across the frame, 0–1, read from get_frame

faceWidth.description: over_shoulder: the head's width ear to ear as a share of the frame width

eyeY.description: over_shoulder: the eyes' height in the frame, 0 = top

opsJson.description: A JSON array of 1 to 50 HyperFrames motion ops in composition seconds: add_animation, stagger, retime, ease, set_keyframes, upsert_keyframe, remove_keyframes, remove_animation, split_text

sourceAssetIds.description: Omit to use enabled timeline videos. An explicit list is exclusive: selected timeline videos keep their pinned versions; new Library videos use their head version.
